title: Rewinding after loading a word
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine with $k>0$ work tapes, designated states $\mathrm{entry}$ and $\mathrm{exit}$, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. For each natural number $j\leq \operatorname{length}(x)$, start the wrapper in phase $1$ with its input head at position $j$, tape zero containing $x$ with its head at position $j-1$, all other work tapes blank with their heads at zero, and empty output. After exactly $j+1$ steps, its configuration is in phase $2$, with its input head at position $1$, tape zero containing $x$ with its head at zero, all other work tapes blank with their heads at zero, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ has at least one work tape
entry and exit are states of $C$
replaced:
For every $j \le |x|$: from the rewind-phase configuration of the decider
wrapper with the full copy of $x$ on tape zero and both active heads just left
of cell $j$, exactly $j + 1$ steps reach the dispatch seam --- the dispatch
state over $x$ on tape zero with all heads at the origin. This includes the
empty input.
